newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PGM ends mixed with nearbys high, gold down.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PGM ends mixed with nearbys high, gold down.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo platinum group metal prices ended mixed with nearby months spiking higher on Thursday, while gold futures ended lower weighed down by the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, traders said.
Trading in nearby months of palladium and distant months moved in opposite directions.

Spot June palladium futures, which has no daily price limit, ended 44 yen per gram higher, while three distant months ended sharply lower before tumbling by their daily 24 yen per gram daily limit temporarily. Benchmark April palladium finished off 19 yen at 565 yen.
"Russia suggested PGM deliveries would resume later this month. But the TOCOM backwardations indicate sharply lower prices later in the year," a commodities analyst said.
Short-term PGM lease rates remained at record high levels.
"The rocketing dollar-based palladium prices forced private investors to cover their massive short-positions, while they built fresh shorts in distant months," he said.
Traders expected PGM prices to be highly volaitle in the near-term, saying it was hard to predict price direction.
Platinum futures ranged from five yen per gram lower to 29 yen higher. Benchmark April was off three yen at 1,377 yen.
Gold futures ranged from 11 yen to 17 yen per gram lower.
Benchmark April was off 17 yen at 1,263 yen.

"The higher PGM prices did not support gold. Market sentiment was undermined by the fact a row between the German Ministry of Finance and the Bundesbank over revaluing gold reserves reached a compromise," one trader said.

In the lacklustre spot market, bullion was little changed at $341.30/70 per ounce at 0739 GMT, against $341.00/50 in New York on Wednesday. Benchmark April silver was down 0.8 yen per 10 grams at 177.2 yen.
